nodes.rationale: Turns one hard-task recording into a demo set per easier same-family task with no re-simulation. Works because Stack, Domino and Sorter tail-extend: the easier task's objects are the first k of the harder one's and the reset draws per object in index order, so the easier rollout is already inside the recording.

nodes.label: tasks/common shared helpers
nodes.rationale: Home of the workbench builder, manipulator wiring, registration seam + PPO cfg, action terms, the one-reward convention, shared observations, absolute-pose reset, SuccessGate, GripperOpenGate, ScatterGrid, the colour palette, the table asset and debug markers - so a category never re-implements them.

nodes.label: Home pose (START_JOINT_POS)
nodes.rationale: ADR-008: reset to an absolute per-joint pose, not mjlab's keyframe-relative offset reset, which sits 1.7 rad away on joints 2 and 3 - that would evaluate a demo-trained policy from a state it had never seen. Contrast with the leader arm's rest pose and the MJCF keyframe.

nodes.label: ScatterGrid (spawn sampler)
nodes.rationale: Collision-free by construction: distinct grid cells, each jittered by less than the half-cell size, so no overlap check is needed. Seed-prefix safe, which is what lets a hard recording be relabelled into easier same-family tasks.

nodes.label: Tail-extension and seed draw ordering
nodes.rationale: Only the hardest task is recorded by hand; easier ones are produced offline. That only works if randomness is drawn easiest-task-first and extended step-wise to the hardest, so the easier task's objects are a prefix of the harder one's and the cutoff lands on a valid state. Data must also be collected in small margins and ordered.

nodes.label: loot-record-demos
nodes.rationale: A GELLO leader arm drives the simulation and the operator labels each episode success or failure with a key; requires leader hardware and a display.

nodes.label: TRLC-DK1 robot asset
nodes.rationale: No public MJCF exists, so dk1.xml was hand-written from the official URDF plus per-color OBJ visual meshes split out of the source GLBs by a one-time converter tool. The gripper is a rack-and-pinion pair coupled by an equality constraint with only gripper_left actuated. Home pose q2=1.7, q3=1.7, q4=-1.5708 puts the downward gripper at about (0.30, 0, 0.20).

nodes.label: Session (one teleop recording run)
nodes.rationale: Recorded into out/demos/success|failure/<task>/<stamp>/ and promoted, when worth keeping, to dataset/demos/<task>/<stamp>/ plus the sibling <stamp>_failure/ - the success/failure split becomes a suffix once kept.

nodes.label: delta_action_from_poses (single build site)
nodes.rationale: The only place a delta action is built. The teleop bridge reaches it through live_bridge/mapper.leader_to_delta_action, so a recorded action and a policy action cannot mean different things; two test modules pin the two halves.

nodes.label: Arm gravity compensation
nodes.rationale: Per-body gravcomp in dk1_constants._compensate_arm_gravity. DiffIK re-anchors its setpoint to the measured pose every substep, so PD sag compounds rather than being corrected - uncompensated, a held zero action walks the arm 0.168 m into the table over 100 steps.

nodes.label: mjlab pinned >=1.5.1,<1.6
nodes.rationale: ADR-003: mjlab 1.6.0 refuses the DK1 collision specification, so no task builds on it. The upper bound is a hard constraint, removable only together with a DK1 asset that compiles on 1.6.

nodes.label: out/ is scratch, dataset/ is kept
nodes.norm_label: out/ is scratch, dataset/ is kept
nodes.rationale: out/ is gitignored and is where the recorder writes; a session worth keeping is moved into the committed dataset/demos/. loot-convert-demos runs against already-kept sessions, so its .npz goes straight to dataset/qc/, committed like the demos it came from.

nodes.label: Action box ([-1, 1] per channel)
nodes.rationale: The clamp is the convention itself, not a safety net: differential IK scales whatever it is handed, so without the clamp DELTA_POS_SCALE would be a unit rather than a bound. Per-channel, not a norm - all three position channels at +-1 is 0.087 m. Quote as '+-5 cm per axis', never '<=5 cm per step'.

nodes.label: BC gate (tests/qc/bc_gate.py)
nodes.rationale: ADR-012: read a demonstration set with a ~2 minute behaviour-cloning fit before spending a whole training run on it. A measurement instrument, not pipeline code: observation in, action chunk out, held-out error back. Runs from the qc venv because it needs JAX.

nodes.label: Closed experiment
nodes.rationale: ADR-014 lists measurements that already removed a suspect (the discount, a dense reward arm, horizon_length=1, a flow_steps sweep, more eval-reset coverage). Running one again measures nothing new.

nodes.label: Control step (0.05 s, 20 Hz)
nodes.rationale: ADR-016: one action per 10 physics steps of 0.005 s. Chosen to match both QC-validated reference domains; the recorded demos set a floor, since at 10 Hz 3% of demo steps stop fitting in one action. Do not call it frame rate or fps.

nodes.label: End-effector delta action
nodes.rationale: First six channels are a pose delta on the grasp site relative to the current pose, solved by differential IK; a zero action holds still. The seventh channel, the gripper, is absolute. Supersedes ADR-005's rule where an action named an absolute joint position.

nodes.label: No last-action observation term
nodes.rationale: It made 'repeat the last action' a trivially strong regressor, so a policy could score on the demos without reading the scene.

nodes.label: cone elliptic, impratio 10
nodes.rationale: Stiffer, less slippery friction than the MuJoCo defaults (pyramidal, 1), which are tuned for locomotion. Taken from the mjlab manipulation example; the grasp test confirms the grip contract - firm hold, no drop, no crush.

nodes.label: Sim profile benchmark campaign
nodes.rationale: Five profiles (train, play, train_acc, mujoco, reference) measured for speed and for qpos deviation from a 1 kHz reference on grasp, sweep and stack rollouts. Headline finding beyond the settings: no profile holds real time on the laptop (train 0.4x, play 0.5x), so laptop teleop always ran in slow motion and the laptop is unsuitable for demo collection regardless of settings. For RL the env is its own ground truth - consistency between demos and training matters, fidelity to a 1 kHz reference does not.

nodes.label: iterations 100 / ls_iterations 50
nodes.rationale: MuJoCo defaults kept instead of mjlab's 10/20 trim. They are free at num_envs=1 - identical speed and trajectories in every scenario, because the solver converges below the caps - and give headroom for contact states where the trimmed caps would silently under-converge. The small limits only matter for thousands of lockstep GPU envs.

nodes.label: timestep 0.005 / decimation 10
nodes.rationale: Accuracy is set by the timestep: 0.01 is measurably the worst (~6x the grasp error, diverges past 1 mm at 0.5 s), 0.005 is sufficient (<=1.5 mm from reference, grip holds, tower stands), 0.002 is more accurate but fixes no observable defect for 32% throughput. decimation was 4 (50 Hz) until ADR-016 moved control to 20 Hz; the physics timestep was deliberately left untouched so the accuracy results still hold.

nodes.label: Success criterion (pure tensor test)

nodes.label: SuccessGate

nodes.label: num_qs must stay at 2 or more
nodes.norm_label: num_qs must stay at 2 or more
nodes.rationale: qc's utils/networks.Value ensemblizes only for num_ensembles > 1, so num_qs=1 returns a critic output with no ensemble axis and every axis=0 aggregation in agents/acfql.py reduces over the batch instead. With actor_type=best-of-n the selected action collapses to a single row and the first update dies on a concatenate shape error. Shrink a critic nothing reads with value_hidden_dims instead.

nodes.label: Adapter (LootEnv gym env)
nodes.rationale: Four load-bearing choices: auto-reset off (mjlab would return the next episode's first observation next to done), corruption off, terminated/truncated kept apart, and observations copied out of simulator memory (mjlab returns a view the next step overwrites).

nodes.label: Contact telemetry (flat info keys)
nodes.rationale: pad_contact_force / object_contact_force are published flat and consumed by name in qc/evaluation.py, which also imports CONTACT_THRESHOLD - a cross-repo contract with no version pin. No success rule reads them; after changing either side, run a short eval and check eval/pad_contact_runs is non-zero.

nodes.label: Convention record (dataset stamp)
nodes.rationale: ADR-011: the stamp (convention name, delta scales, gripper mapping, control step, start-pose noise, task id; qc/dataset.STAMP_KEYS) is compared against the environment a run builds and raises on mismatch, including a missing stamp. It exists because the failure it guards is silent: the loss falls and evaluation scores zero.

nodes.label: Seam (loot_bench/qc/)
nodes.rationale: ADR-002 and ADR-009: training lives in a separate upstream qc checkout, and this repo holds only the gym adapter, the demo converter and the dataset contract. The seam changes no part of the MDP, because the recorder must see exactly the MDP the trainer sees.

nodes.label: Start-pose noise
nodes.rationale: Uniform half-width around the home pose, default 0.0. A run can override with train_qc.sh --start_pose_noise or LOOT_START_POSE_NOISE, but the dataset stamp then has to agree or the load aborts. Keep any value inside the recorder's alignment gate, which is one action box wide. Measure start-state variety with peak-to-peak range, never standard deviation.

nodes.label: MIN_GRIP_FORCE release check (0.1 N)
nodes.rationale: The gripper-joint check alone can be fooled by a wedged grasp that still grips past the open threshold, so the measured finger-pad contact force runs alongside it.

nodes.label: Ball category
nodes.rationale: Chosen to evaluate dynamics (apply enough force to reach a goal outside direct reach) and long-horizon credit assignment (the reward arrives substantially after the action).

nodes.label: Stack category
nodes.rationale: Only the final height matters, not block position, and every variant carries 2n blocks - more than the minimum - so staircases and pyramids are viable strategies. The footprint stays square because blocks spawn at a random yaw, making the variation axis exactly the height:width ratio; mass follows the shape via BLOCK_DENSITY, so the slenderest block is also the lightest. Blocks within a variant are identical, so exactly n of them reach the target and no other count does.

nodes.label: Throw task
nodes.rationale: Throw the ball over a wall to a target; whether reduced gravity is needed is still open.

nodes.label: Splitter self-check on recomputed reward
nodes.rationale: The splitter reproduces the environment's one-step reward lag and its held-block progress exclusion, then recomputes the source episode's own reward and compares it to the recording. When an observation layout, a success kernel or the gripper's open threshold changes, that self-check is what fails - fix the splitter, do not loosen the tolerance.

nodes.label: Reward lag (one control step)
nodes.rationale: mjlab runs the reward and termination managers before the command manager, so success in step k is paid at step k+1. The lag is identical when recording and when evaluating, so it cancels - never correct it on one side alone.

nodes.label: Shortfall floor (MIN_SHORTFALL 1e-3)
nodes.rationale: A task can report full progress before the success gate latches; without the floor that step reads a true zero, which QC's --sparse mapping ((rewards != 0.0) * -1.0) would relabel a success.

nodes.label: Task reward (one term, [-1, 0])
nodes.rationale: ADR-006: exactly one reward term at weight 1.0, no shaping terms and no penalties. It stays in [-1, 0] and reads exactly 0 only at success, because every task ends on success and a positive per-step reward would pay a policy to hover at the goal and never touch it. Old name 'reward mode' (a tier of progress + success terms) is deliberately avoided.

nodes.label: Ball sparse reward (-1 until it scores)
nodes.norm_label: ball sparse reward (-1 until it scores)
nodes.rationale: No progress signal: a ball is either in the target zone or not, and the distance says little about where the throw will land. The command tracks the target relative to the field's live pose, not as a constant offset, because the field pose is itself randomized.

nodes.label: Stack progress (tallest resting block)
nodes.rationale: ADR-017: a block held in the gripper is excluded, so lifting one to the target height earns nothing until it is released - otherwise a policy could farm progress by hovering a block at height.

nodes.label: nativeccd disabled (analytic box-box collider)
nodes.rationale: In MuJoCo Warp the flag has exactly one effect: box-box pairs are rerouted from the generic GJK/EPA convex pipeline (<=4 contacts sharing one depth and normal frame) to the analytic collider (up to 8 contacts with individual depths and normals). That difference is why cube stacking and box-pad grasping jittered with it on; disabling it globally is harmless because it is inert for every non-box-box pair.

nodes.label: Evaluated-capabilities framing
nodes.rationale: Each category is justified by the capability it isolates (long-horizon precision, robustness, precision, combinatorial complexity, strategy, dynamics, long-horizon credit assignment) rather than by scene variety, so the suite covers distinct axes.

Its two randomness axes (cube spawn, target) are pinned or sampled independently, so FixedS-FixedT is the smallest learnable version.

nodes.label: Automatic registration via package discovery
nodes.rationale: tasks/__init__.py calls mjlab's import_packages once with blacklist ['utils', '.mdp', 'common', 'peg_insertion']; the .mdp/common entries stop MDP and shared-helper modules being scanned as task configs, and peg_insertion is archived and unregistered. A single 'import loot_bench' therefore registers everything.

nodes.label: Task category pattern
nodes.rationale: Every category mirrors the same layout (variants.py, assets.py, mdp/, <cat>_env_cfg.py, config/__init__.py) so adding or editing one means copying an existing one rather than inventing a structure.

nodes.label: Keep-out (blocked_near)
nodes.rationale: Cells within a clearance of a goal are blocked, because an object dropped on its own target is awkward to align from there. The keep_free argument holds back enough cells that an env is never left with fewer cells than objects.

nodes.label: Recovery demonstration
nodes.rationale: ADR-013 proposed recordings starting off the ideal path, near the states a rollout really visits, as the answer to demonstrations too far apart to interpolate between - and rejected it for now in favour of pinning the spawn and target instead. None has been recorded.

nodes.label: Domino progress (build / topple phases)
nodes.rationale: KnockOver variants split the interval: half the placement fraction while building, then half placement plus half toppled during the topple phase. Row spacing is always fixed so the knock-over stays possible even in RandomRow.

nodes.label: Place progress (spawn-to-target travel)
nodes.rationale: Normalized by the constant MAX_TRAVEL_DIST rather than anything per-episode, so the reward scale does not shift with the sampled distance. NOTE - episode length is stated inconsistently across the repo: rl_settings.md says 500 steps, while CLAUDE.md says 15 s i.e. 300 steps at 20 Hz. CLAUDE.md is the higher-authority file; the discrepancy is unresolved.

nodes.label: Fixed prop
nodes.rationale: A MjSpec body with no free joint, auto-wrapped by mjlab as a mocap body; positioned via EntityCfg init_state rather than spec body pos, because mjlab overwrites a fixed-base root body's pose from init_state.

nodes.label: Shared proprioceptive observation group
nodes.rationale: Joint positions, joint velocities and the end-effector pose in every task; actor and critic read the same terms.

nodes.label: Explicit actuator split (arm / gripper / ik_max_dq)
nodes.rationale: All three fields are required. Deriving the arm as 'every actuator that is not the gripper' was rejected because it makes the residue load-bearing: a later robot's torso or wrist-camera joint would silently join the IK chain. ik_max_dq is a torque cap (kp x max_dq), not a rate limit.

nodes.label: ee_pose publishes a 6D rotation
nodes.rationale: ADR-007: the term is 9 wide (position plus the first two columns of the rotation matrix). mjlab's quat_from_matrix picks its branch with an argmax over candidates that tie, and the DK1 grasp site sits on that tie, so float noise flipped the sign of one smooth motion on 14 of 120 steps. Body poses keep their quaternion because data.xquat is integrated continuously.

nodes.label: ManipulatorInterface
nodes.rationale: Declares name, entity-cfg factory, grasp site, gripper joints + open threshold, end-effector subtree, finger-pad geom regex, viewer body and start pose. It carries no action scale - those are shared constants - so supporting a new robot is adding one interface instance.

nodes.label: Observations carry no noise
nodes.rationale: ADR-015: observation noise is a robustness device for an on-policy run that collects its own data. Training is offline from demonstrations that came through the uncorrupted observation, so noise would split the offline and online halves apart. actor and critic are now the same terms. If sim-to-real robustness is ever wanted, put it in one place (make_manipulation_env_cfg) and re-record the demonstrations through it.

nodes.label: Released (robot has let go)
nodes.rationale: Gripper-joint opening for cube/insertion tasks; ball-to-grasp-site distance for ball, because a thrown or putted ball leaves the gripper and the gripper can be in any state afterwards.

nodes.label: Wiring (robot into task cfg)
nodes.rationale: The single seam between tasks and robots: tasks stay robot-agnostic and read everything from a ManipulatorInterface.

nodes.label: Workbench (shared env skeleton)
nodes.rationale: One shared tabletop skeleton (table, proprioception, one task reward, success/time-out episode) so a category only builds its category-shaped parts.

nodes.label: Ball distance-based release test
nodes.rationale: The ball counts as released once it is more than _RELEASE_DISTANCE from the grasp site, because a thrown or putted ball leaves the gripper and the gripper's own state says nothing afterwards.
